event_id.description: Unique identifier for this event, used for idempotency and threading.

thread_id.description: Groups events belonging to one orchestration run.

in_reply_to.description: event_id this event responds to, if any.

relayed_by.description: Human-relay agents that touched this event en route, in order. Present for auditability when a message crosses more than one relay hop.

agent_id.description: Stable label for this agent within the run, e.g. 'planner', 'implementer', 'reviewer-human'.

role.description: Required when kind=human, absent when kind=llm. Replaces the human-relay and human-participant members of the pre-registry surface enum, which allowed the meaningless combination kind=llm with surface=human-relay.

surface.description: Namespaced vendor:surface identifier resolvable in orchestration/registry/. Descriptive label for humans and for registry lookup. Where it disagrees with 'capability', capability governs and the mismatch is worth surfacing rather than silently resolving. Omit for kind=human.

capability.description: Normative. Every routing and gating decision in this system reads these fields rather than the surface name.

regime.description: Derived from 'capability' by the three-clause rule in taxonomy.md. Stated explicitly so a receiving agent without the surface-regimes skill still sees it, and so the derivation is checkable against the capability profile rather than asserted.

active_skills.description: Operator-side behavioral configuration identifiers active for this agent. Format is vendor-defined. An empty array is valid and expected for vendors with no skill mechanism. A mismatch between this field and a receiving agent's own inference is worth surfacing rather than silently resolving.

capability_profile.description: Vendor-independent predicates. Any surface from any vendor scores on all seven.

interface.description: Whether the surface presents a conversational loop or is driven by a caller-owned program.

autonomy.description: Autonomous multi-step execution between human turns. 'redirectable' means the human can interrupt and steer mid-task.

human_presence.description: Whether a human is present during execution.

workspace.description: Persistent file workspace. 'session' means state exists but is lost at session end.

tool_execution.description: Whether the surface executes tools, and whether execution reaches the host filesystem. Read by the routing rule's standing tool-call exclusion.

egress.description: Where content goes when this surface processes it. This is the sensitivity gate's join key: a routing rule can read this field instead of relying on an operator remembering which faculties are cloud-hosted.

audit.description: Who, if anyone, attests to a record of what this surface did. 'unknown' is a legitimate and common value; do not guess.
